title: U.S. House · Texas's 2nd District
area: Harris and Montgomery counties, including The Woodlands and parts of northeast Houston

context.text: State Representative Steve Toth defeated incumbent U.S. Representative Dan Crenshaw in the March 3, 2026 Republican primary, 55.8% to 40.7%. Crenshaw is not on the November general-election ballot.

candidates.name: Shaun Finnie
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary unopposed

summary.text: Shaun Finnie is the Democratic nominee for Texas's 2nd Congressional District and an investment banker who, by his own account, spent about 30 years in energy mergers and acquisitions after a brief career as an oil and gas lawyer. In his Ballotpedia survey he lists his priorities as reducing tariffs and health care costs, expanding the Affordable Care Act, education funding, and bipartisan immigration reform.

background.text: In his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, he says he grew up on a farm in a family of modest means, was raised with his two siblings by his mother, a registered nurse who worked two jobs, and was the first in his family to attend college.

According to the same survey, he earned a bachelor's degree in economics from the University of Saskatchewan, a law degree from the University of Western Ontario, and an MBA in finance and accounting from Northwestern University. (Ballotpedia's summary infobox lists Northwestern for all his degrees.)
Describes working as an oil and gas lawyer for three years, then spending roughly 30 years in investment banking focused on energy, primarily oil and gas mergers and acquisitions.
Says he and his wife have lived in The Woodlands for 20 years and raised four children there.
Says he served on the Board of Trustees of The John Cooper School for several years and founded an investment club for high school students, teaching personal finance to students for seven years.
Won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary for Texas's 2nd District unopposed, according to Ballotpedia's results listing, and faces Republican Steve Toth in the general election.

priorities.text: Says he supports eliminating tariffs he describes as a driver of inflation, raising the minimum wage, and lowering healthcare costs.
Supports expanding the Affordable Care Act, calling it "the most important piece of legislation passed in this century."

positions.summary: Says tariffs are a major driver of inflation and supports getting rid of them.
positions.quote: Tariffs are one of the most obvious drivers of inflation, costing the average American family $2,000–$3,000 a year. I believe in getting rid of harmful tariffs, raising the minimum wage, and lowering healthcare costs so working families have a real opportunity to achieve the American Dream.

positions.summary: Says he supports raising the minimum wage as part of improving affordability.
positions.quote: I believe in getting rid of harmful tariffs, raising the minimum wage, and lowering healthcare costs

positions.summary: Supports expanding the Affordable Care Act and opposes Republican efforts to scale it back.
positions.quote: If we allow Republicans to keep chipping away at the ACA, healthcare will become unaffordable for millions of Americans. I will do everything I can to expand the ACA and make healthcare as accessible and affordable as possible for families across this country.

candidates.researchNotes: Biography comes mainly from Finnie's own Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, which gives no birthplace or year of birth; no news profile was found.

candidates.name: Steve Toth
candidates.ballotNote: Defeated incumbent U.S. Rep. Dan Crenshaw in the March 3, 2026 Republican primary
candidates.currentRole: Member, Texas House of Representatives (since 2019; also served 2013–2015)

summary.text: Steve Toth is a Republican member of the Texas House of Representatives from The Woodlands area, an ordained pastor and small business owner. He served one term in the Texas House (2013-2015), ran unsuccessfully for the Texas Senate in 2014 and for Congress in 2016, and returned to the Texas House in 2019. In March 2026 he defeated Rep. Dan Crenshaw in the Republican primary for Texas's 2nd District; his campaign website describes him as a conservative who will take that record to Washington.

background.text: Born in New York on November 29, 1960, and raised near Rochester, where he attended Pittsford Mendon High School and Rochester Bible College, according to Wikipedia.

Describes himself as an ordained pastor and small business owner. He owns the residential pool companies Acclaim Pools and My PoolXpert in The Woodlands; earlier sales, marketing and business development work included Johnson & Johnson, Apple Orthodontix and Harris Interactive.
First elected to Texas House District 15 in 2012 after defeating five-term Republican incumbent Rob Eissler in the primary, and served from January 2013 to January 2015.

Ran in the 2014 special election for Texas Senate District 4, finishing second to Brandon Creighton and losing the August 2014 runoff, 67% to 33%. In 2016 he challenged U.S. Rep. Kevin Brady in the Republican primary for Texas's 8th Congressional District and received 37.4% to Brady's 53.4%.

Returned to Texas House District 15 in 2019 after the previous holder, Mark Keough, did not seek re-election, and has been re-elected since; he is not running for re-election to the Texas House in 2026.

In the Texas House, his Ballotpedia profile lists committee assignments including Appropriations (listed in every term from 2019 to 2024), Culture, Recreation and Tourism (2019-2020), Agriculture and Livestock (2021-2022) and Corrections (2023-2024). His campaign website says he authored legislation banning Critical Race Theory and the social transitioning of children in Texas schools and helped secure border security funding as a member of the Appropriations Committee.
Announced his campaign for Congress in July 2025 and defeated incumbent Rep. Dan Crenshaw and two other candidates in the March 3, 2026 Republican primary, 55.8% to 40.7% for Crenshaw.
According to his campaign website, he and his wife, Babette, have been married for over 40 years and are parents and grandparents; he lives in Montgomery County, Texas.

priorities.text: Says "family, faith, and freedom are the cornerstones of America" and describes his legislative record as consistently among the most conservative in the Texas House.

candidates.researchNotes: Ballotpedia's curated key messages for Toth focus on general conservative positioning rather than specific policy statements on the issue list; no specific stance quotes on listed issues were found in the sources checked.
